note: Ližnjan came third of eighteen towns in the rebuilt record sweep, behind only Rijeka and Svetvinčenat, and this archive had never given it a page. It got one because of a pin on a map — a line David had drawn years ago from Ližnjan to Monheim in Bavaria, with a note beside it reading «Grga dies in Zagreb», and no source of any kind.
lead: Grga turns out to be real, and the register holds two generations of his family.

grga.heading: Grga — Gregorius Defranceski of Ližnjan, born 1851

rows.lab: His marriage, and his age in it
rows.text: A marriage at Ližnjan on **10 June 1874**. The principal is **Gregorius Defranceski**, and the clerk records his age: **22**, which puts his birth in 1851. The record is filed under Croatia-Slavonia, Magyarország — the Hungarian half of the Monarchy — with the place tagged Ližnjan, Istria.

**Maria Vojnić.** She is named as the mother in every one of his children's baptisms. Vojnić is one of the great Ližnjan surnames — and it is one of the names standing beside «Defrančeski Ante» in the «Pučki prijatelj» subscription list of 27 February 1920.

**Gregorio Defranceschi and Agata Skifić**, who appear across the Ližnjan books from the 1840s. The indexer has repeatedly merged the two surnames into «Gregorii Skifić» and «Agathæ Skifić», which is how a machine reads a Latin entry giving a father, a mother and her maiden name in one line. Read against the Italian-language entries of the same couple — «Gregorio Defranceschi» and «Agata Schiffich» — the household is unmistakable.

rows.lab: His children, from the baptism book
rows.text: **Anastasia**, baptised 23 February 1875 and again a child of the same name on 23 February 1876 — the second almost certainly named for the first. **Maria**, born 4 January 1878, baptised the 5th. **Justina**, born 3 October 1879, baptised the 4th. **Maria** again, born 25 January 1882, baptised the 26th — so the 1878 Maria had died. And **Josephus**, March 1887. Six baptisms in thirteen years and at least two of them replacing a dead child, which is the ordinary arithmetic of an Istrian village.

**Justina Defrančeski** — spelt there with the háček — married **Josephus Fedel** at Ližnjan on 22 November 1898. **Stana Defranceski** married **Jacobus Vojnić** on 7 August 1899. Two Ližnjan houses, in two years.

Gregorio and Agata's own children run back to the 1840s: Maria, 8 December 1846; Cattarina, 31 October 1847; a Giovanni; Agatha, born 30 December 1867 and baptised on New Year's Day 1868; a Maria who married Josephus Ruman on 17 November 1869; and a Lucia who married Joannes Sandalj on 11 February 1874, four months before her brother's wedding. Behind them stands a **Mattio De Franceschi** with a wife **Madalena Peucovich**, given as Gregorio's own parents.

rows.lab: A death that may be his sister's
rows.text: At Ližnjan on 6 October 1879, a **Lucia** died aged twenty-five, born 1854, buried the next day. The indexer could not tell from the page whether her husband was «Joannis Sandalj» or «Gregorii Defranceski» and wrote both. If she is the Lucia Defranceschi who married Joannes Sandalj in February 1874, then Grga buried his sister five years into her marriage and three days after his daughter Justina was baptised.

grga.source_g: FamilySearch record indexes for Ližnjan, Istria — 127 entries of this surname recovered in a targeted sweep, September 2026, spanning 1788 to the twentieth century. The marriage of 10 June 1874 is ark 1:1:XQM3-BLWJ; the baptism of 26 January 1882 is 1:1:XQM3-B4YH; the burial of 7 October 1879 is 1:1:XQM3-G3KW. Index entries, not images: the parish books themselves are at Pazin and have not been read.

monheim.heading: Monheim and Zagreb — corrected the same evening, by David's own tree

rows.text: Two Gregorios at Ližnjan, either side of the one found here. **Gregorio de Franceschi, born 23 May 1822 at Ližnjan, died there 25 November 1861** — old enough to be the father of the Gregorius who married in 1874 at twenty-two. And **Gregorius «Grgo» Defranceski, born 1931 at Ližnjan, died at Zagreb** — the man on the pin. Four generations of the name in one village, and the family knew about the last of them all along.

A line drawn from Ližnjan to **Monheim**, and a separate pin, «Petar Moves to Metzingen». The coordinates on the Monheim pin are 10.8537 E, 48.8427 N — which is **Monheim in Bavaria**, in the Donau-Ries, not Monheim am Rhein. It matters: Bavarian Monheim is about a hundred kilometres from Metzingen, and Metzingen is four kilometres from Pfullingen, where this family's own wartime papers were issued.

rows.lab: And what carries no source at all
rows.text: Nothing. The pin has no note, no date, no name and no document behind it, and neither does «Grga dies in Zagreb». They are David's own knowledge, drawn on a map some years ago. This archive has searched for both and found neither: no Defranceschi at Monheim in any index reachable from here, and no death for a Grga at Zagreb in the newspapers or the burial indexes.

rows.lab: And then David's own tree answered it, and this archive had the wrong man
rows.text: Read directly out of the live MyHeritage tree the same evening: **«Gregorius ‘Grgo’ Defranceski, born 1931 at Ližnjan, died at Zagreb.»** That is the Grga of the map pin, and he is not the Gregorius born in 1851 whom this page had just reconstructed out of the registers. He is four generations later. The pin was right and the reading of it here was wrong: this archive found *a* Grga at Ližnjan, decided it must be the one, and had to be corrected by the tree.

The Ližnjan parish registers at the Državni arhiv u Pazinu, read as images rather than as an index — for Grga's own baptism about 1851, his death, and any emigration note in the margin. And Zagreb's Mirogoj burial records for Marija Defrančeski, 1884–1971, which would give a birthplace.

why: Three things follow. The first is that a map pin with no source is worth chasing: Grga existed, and a whole household came back with him. The second is that this archive got the identification wrong — it found a Gregorius at Ližnjan and assumed he was the one, when the man on the pin was born eighty years later. That correction came from the family's own tree, not from the archive's cleverness, and it is left standing here rather than quietly rewritten. The third is unchanged: Monheim still carries no source of any kind, and stays unverified on this page in the same size type as everything else.
